data.name: Ihram
data.gender_notes: Ihram is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The state of purity and intention assumed by Muslims before entering the Grand Mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia for the Hajj pilgrimage. The name Ihram carries the meaning “Sanctified State” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ihram usually hope their child will grow to embody sanctified state and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of devotion, purity, and commitment to one's faith.
data.etymology: Ihram belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sanctified State.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ihram total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The wearing of the Ihram attire is a symbol of unity and equality among pilgrims, regardless of race, nationality, or social status, as they all don the same simple clothing. The Ihram also serves as a reminder of the spiritual journey ahead, encouraging pilgrims to focus on their intentions for the pilgrimage and maintain a humble, reverent mindset.
data.spiritual_significance: The Ihram represents the purification of the soul and body, signifying the spiritual preparation for the Hajj pilgrimage. This state of spiritual purity and intention reflects the fundamental Islamic belief in submission to Allah and seeking His favor, as well as emphasizing the importance of honoring and upholding Islamic values and rituals throughout the journey. The state of Ihram also serves as a reminder of the temporary nature of worldly possessions and worldly life, highlighting the importance of living a purposeful and worshipful life guided by faith and seeking forgiveness from Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Sanctified State" symbolizes The state of purity and intention assumed by Muslims before entering the Grand Mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia for the Hajj pilgrimage.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ihram serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of sanctified state.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Vol. 3, p. 261. This source relates that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) wore the Ihram during the Farewell Pilgrimage in 632 AD, which was the last pilgrimage he led, in commemoration of the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham, pbuh) and his son Isma'il (Ishmael, pbuh) who wore the Ihram during their pilgrimage to build the Ka'bah.

Al-Baladhuri, Ansab Al-Ashraf, Vol. 2, p. 275. This source relates that the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) declared the Ihram a sacred state in the lifetime of the Prophet, and that it should be observed at the specified times, namely, the two sacred months of Hajj and 'Umrah.
historical_references.time_period: During the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
historical_references.context: Declaration of Ihram as a sacred state

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Ihram' originates from Islamic tradition, where it refers to the state of purity and preparation for performing the Hajj pilgrimage. In modern contexts, this term is frequently used across various digital platforms to discuss and showcase different aspects of the Hajj experience. On Instagram, accounts dedicated to travel and fashion often share breathtaking images and videos of the pilgrimage sites, as well as stylish Ihram outfits. On TikTok, short video clips show the journey and experiences of pilgrims in real-time. Pinterest boards feature carefully curated collections of inspirational images and informative articles about the Hajj and Ihram, appealing to those planning or interested in the spiritual pilgrimage.
